name: Ribeye Meatballs on Mashed Potatoes
desc: Large ground ribeye meatballs poached in a chunky onion and tomato marinara, served over olive oil mashed potatoes.

source.title: Ribeye Meatballs on Mashed Potatoes
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp kosher salt, for the cooking water

steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot with the salt and cover with cold water by 4 inches. Bring to a boil, then simmer rapidly about 15 minutes, until they fall apart when poked.

Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a wide, deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, 5-6 minutes. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook 3 minutes, then add the marinara and bring to a simmer.
Gently mix the ribeye with the salt, pepper and paprika and roll into 8 large meatballs (about 3 oz each). Do not pack them tight.
Drop the raw meatballs into the simmering sauce and spoon sauce over them. Cover and simmer over medium-low 25-30 minutes, turning once, until they read 160°F in the center.
Reserve 1 cup of potato water, then drain the potatoes and return them to the pot for a minute to steam dry. Mash with the olive oil and enough reserved water to make them creamy. Season with salt.
Spoon the mash onto plates, top with meatballs and sauce, and finish with cilantro, green onions and flaky salt.
tips: Mash by hand; a blender or food processor turns potatoes gluey.
The caption lists olive oil with the potatoes; RecipeTin Eats' classic mash uses 4 tbsp butter and 1/2 cup warm milk per 3 lb potatoes if you want a richer version.
The caption names "baby onions" as a garnish; sliced green onions or halved pearl onions both fit.
